findings.title: Deposit is within the amount cap
findings.detail: This amount check does not verify deposit protection or authenticity. Annual rent GBP 15600; cap = 15600 / 52 * 5 (GBP 1500.00 rounded down to pennies); requested GBP 1500. Importance: 85/100. Conditional: Confirm that the rented property is in England. Confirm this is an ordinary private tenancy, not an excluded arrangement. Confirm that rent and deposit cover the same whole tenancy. The amount calculation is sound on the quoted figures: rent of GBP 1300 per calendar month gives annual rent of GBP 15,600, and five weeks is GBP 1,500.00. The stated deposit of GBP 1500 equals the cap, so it is not over it. The cap applies only to covered tenancies. Jurisdiction, tenancy type and whether rent and deposit relate to the same whole tenancy are all unknown in the context, and no answers were supplied. The conclusion therefore remains conditional rather than a confirmed pass. The contract gives no counter-evidence that defeats the amount check, so dismissal is not warranted. This amount check says nothing about deposit protection or authenticity. Sources: https://www.gov.uk/guidance/tenant-fees-act-2019-guidance-for-tenants

questions: Is this a private tenancy in England with the landlord living elsewhere?
What rent period and tenancy does the deposit cover, and can the amount be revised?

findings.title: Whether Northbank Example Lettings Ltd is still an active company: two parts of agency check disagree
findings.detail:
Agency check says The official company register lists the company as dissolved ("company_status: dissolved"). Agency check says The agent told you in your messages that the company is actively registered ("We are actively registered."). The agent's statement and the official register cannot both be true. This affects whether the company named in your contract can lawfully act, and who you would be paying or sending documents to.
Source: https://find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/company/96779816
